'''Klaus Peter Grohe''' (born 16 January 1934) is a German [[chemist]] best known for pioneering work on [[quinolone]] and [[fluoroquinolone antibiotics]] at [[Bayer|Bayer AG]], including the invention of [[Ciprofloxacin]]. He developed a widely adopted [[chemical synthesis|synthetic]] approach known as the "Grohe method" for constructing quinolone [[carboxylic acid]]s, which underpinned later [[fluoroquinolone]] discovery programs. In retirement, he and his wife established the '''Klaus Grohe Foundation''' (''Klaus-Grohe-Stiftung'') to support young researchers in drug discovery and medicinal chemistry.<ref name=gdch2020>{{cite web|url=https://www.gdch.de/fileadmin/downloads/GDCh/Preise_und_Auszeichnungen/PDF/grohe_2020.pdf|title=The Klaus Grohe Foundation|publisher=German Chemical Society (GDCh)|date=2020|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref><ref name=gdch>{{cite web|url=https://en.gdch.de/gdch/foundations/klaus-grohe-foundation.html|title=Klaus Grohe Foundation|publisher=GDCh|date=17 April 2025|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref><ref name=heravi2020>{{cite journal|last=Heravi|first=M.M.|title=Prescribed drugs containing nitrogen heterocycles|journal=RSC Advances|year=2020|volume=10|issue=72 |pages=44247–44311|doi=10.1039/D0RA01826F|doi-broken-date=26 September 2025 |pmid=35557843 |pmc=9092475 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Grohe was born in [[Ludwigshafen am Rhein]] on 16 January 1934. He studied chemistry at the [[University of Würzburg]], where he completed a doctorate in 1964 on the synthesis of [[pyridine]] derivatives.<ref name=gdch2020/>

== Career ==
Grohe joined the main research laboratory of Bayer in [[Leverkusen]] in 1965. After early work on [[organochlorine]] and [[organofluorine]] intermediates he moved into heterocycle synthesis for pharmaceutical research. In the 1970s he devised a new cyclocondensation strategy using ''o''-halo(aroyl) halides to access quinoline and azaquinoline carboxylic acids—an approach that became known as the '''Grohe method'''.<ref name=gdch2020/> This methodology enabled the synthesis, in April 1981, of the fluoroquinolone antibiotics [[ciprofloxacin]] and [[enrofloxacin]].

Grohe is named as an inventor on core ciprofloxacin patents, including US 4,670,444 (reexamined as US 4,670,444 B1).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US4670444B1/en|title=US4670444B1 — quinoline/naphthyridine-3-carboxylic acids|website=Google Patents|date=1987|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref> Court records from patent litigation in the United States have described the synthetic route and prior steps leading to ciprofloxacin within Bayer's program.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.finnegan.com/files/Publication/05e69900-a607-4e6a-ab6e-b4ed5a2989f3/Presentation/PublicationAttachment/783fd0cf-e3e7-4a32-9ee7-bb90d7a42696/01-1286-080902.pdf|title=Bayer AG v. Schein Pharmaceutical, Inc. — Federal Circuit (2002)|website=Finnegan|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/district-courts/FSupp2/129/705/2471435/|title=Bayer AG v. Schein Pharmaceutical, Inc., 129 F.Supp.2d 705 (E.D.N.Y. 2001)|website=Justia|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref>

He retired from Bayer in 1997.<ref name=gdch2020/>

== Research and impact ==
According to the [[German Chemical Society]], "nearly all modern fluoroquinolone antibiotics are synthesized using the Grohe method," and subsequent optimization under Grohe's supervision at Bayer contributed to later agents such as [[moxifloxacin]] and [[pradofloxacin]].<ref name=gdch2020/> Reviews of drug-discovery history and heterocycle-based medicines also credit Grohe's role in the origin of ciprofloxacin.<ref name=heravi2020/>

== Awards and honors ==
* [[Otto Bayer]] Medal (1987), for work leading to the synthesis of ciprofloxacin; and again (2001) for lifetime achievements.<ref name=gdch2020/>
* Cross of Merit 1st Class of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]] (2005).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bildungsklick.de/bundeslaender/detail/leverkusener-forscher-fuer-seine-erfindungen-ausgezeichnet|title=Leverkusener Forscher für seine Erfindungen ausgezeichnet|website=bildungsklick|date=9 December 2005|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref>
* Honorary title ''[[Professor]]'' conferred by the [[North_Rhine-Westphalia | State of North Rhine-Westphalia]] (2010).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bayer.com/sites/default/files/the-grohe-method-and-quinolone-antibiotics.pdf|title=The Grohe method and quinolone antibiotics|publisher=Bayer|date=2020|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref>

== Philanthropy ==
In 2001 Grohe and his wife Eva established the '''Klaus Grohe Foundation''' at the [[German Chemical Society]] (GDCh). The foundation has awarded the '''Klaus Grohe Prize''' (since 2020 the '''Klaus Grohe Award''') for outstanding work in drug discovery; since 2020 it has been endowed with €50,000 and focuses on scientists working in Europe.<ref name=gdch /> Grohe and his wife also endowed the '''Eva and Klaus Grohe Prize''' ([[Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]), awarded in 2003–2015 for achievements in infectiology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbaw.de/die-akademie/auszeichnungen/ehemals-verliehene-preise/eva-und-klaus-grohe-preis-der-akademie|title=Eva und Klaus Grohe-Preis der Akademie|publisher=Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref>

* Formulations containing ciprofloxacin and related actives, US 4,844,902.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/0c/34/6a/3226cff1590dd8/US4844902.pdf|title=US 4,844,902|website=USPTO|date=1989|access-date=23 August 2025}}</ref>
